correctness.rationale: For every finite cyclic state group and arbitrary active subset, H-equivariance forces each word image to contain a whole H-coset, giving rank at least |H|. The induced quotient mask has trivial stabilizer. Given an oriented pair gap d, a rotating placement at an active u with u+d inactive followed by b reduces d to d-1; repeated reductions merge all quotient states. Lifting gives rank <=|H|, exact. Primitive-root counting by Möbius inversion proves both unweighted and fixed-weight formulas including zero/full masks. Replayed standalone checker: exhaustive exact subset-BFS of 1020 automata n=2..9, 65532 masks n=2..15, 449 weighted formula cases, 1320 constructive replays, 394 stride masks. Checks do not substitute for the induction.

originality.rationale: Full primary manuscript of Kari–Ryzhikov–Varonka, DOI:10.1007/978-3-030-24886-4_5, studies word-length bounds and prescribed-rank circular examples, not the exact rank for arbitrary partial-successor masks. Full papers of Volkov, Rystsov–Szykuła, and Hoffmann have sufficient synchronization or complete-reachability results but lack this stabilizer-specific full-mask classifier. Exact-result and alias queries did not identify stronger covering statements; search absence alone is not claimed as proof of novelty. Standard prime/one-active cases and necklace counting as such are not claimed new.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier formulation using different semigroup or cyclic-pattern terminology could imply the result; no complete novelty guarantee is available.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete natural classification over all \(2^n\) binary active masks, a direct finite symmetry invariant computing the smallest achievable state uncertainty, a synchronizability criterion without subset search, and exact counts by rank and active-set size. Unlike generic estimates of the length of minimum-rank words, it answers which ranks occur and exactly how often, distinguishing primitive underlying digraphs with periodic-mask obstructions. The exact invariant is motivated by state compression in circular automata; this is not a selected small-n table or an arbitrary parameter slice.
